items.note: DETECTOR CAUTION on this source. The Maersk routing API exposes a boolean isRoutingAdhoc. On CNYTN-USHOU it is true only for this XL row and false for all eight TP15 rows, which looks like a clean ad-hoc label. On KRPUS-USHOU it is true for EVERY row including all eight TP15 proforma sailings. It therefore behaves like a per-pair routing attribute, not an ad-hoc marker, and must be treated as context only - the same way isGemini is - never as a trigger. This voyage stays classified as an extra loader on the strength of the serviceName XL / serviceCode 770 being absent from every alliance registry, not on that flag. vsProforma uses the modal TP15 transit observed this run (33 days across 4 of 8 sailings); the 17 Sep record used 34, so the 1-day move in deltaDays is a proforma-side change, not a slip.

AUG is Evergreen marketing for the Premier Alliance EC4 Asia-US Gulf service, not an Ocean Alliance code and not an Evergreen solo service. Evidence this run: TVS2_VesselSchedule for EVER LUCKY 085E returns LINE Asia-U.S. GULF Service(AUG) with rotation Kaohsiung / Cai Mep / Yantian / Ningbo / Pusan / Panama Canal / Houston / Mobile and a matching 085W westbound leg, while the ONE Route Finder returns the same two ships, ONE ARCADIA 079E ETD 2026-10-01 and EVER LUCKY 085E ETD 2026-10-07, as EC4 direct on CNYTN-USHOU. AUG moved from Ocean Alliance plus a stray Evergreen solo bucket into Premier Alliance alongside EC4. AUG is NOT an extra loader.

MSC CNYTN-USHOU: within the registry service LONE STAR EXPRESS, one sailing carries an off-pattern voyage number, ROTTERDAM 87E departing 2026-10-12, against GN637E through GN644E for every other vessel on the string. Not published as an extra loader because detection is keyed on service code and LONE STAR is a registry service with no ad-hoc label. Flagged for the next run: if a second off-pattern voyage appears on the same string, it is worth a workup.

Lanes and sources not covered this run: (1) Evergreen second pass with departureDay +28 was not run - ss.shipmentlink.com returned ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED after the twelfth query, so Evergreen visibility this run is 4 weeks (to 19 Oct 2026), not the full 8-week window. (2) Hapag-Lloyd Cai Mep: both VNCMT and VNTOT returned HTTP 400, lane not covered. (3) Maersk CNYTN-USNYC, CNSHA-USNYC and KRPUS-USNYC returned HTTP 422 and CNTAO-USHOU returned HTTP 400; Maersk USEC coverage this run is limited to CNNGB-USSAV and CNYTN-USSAV. (4) MSC covered only CNYTN-USHOU and CNYTN-USNYC. (5) ONE covered only CNYTN-USNYC, CNSHA-USNYC and CNYTN-USHOU, stopped deliberately at three lanes before the Thanks for Your Patience gate. (6) CMA CGM covered only CNYTN-USHOU and CNYTN-USNYC.
